matching_note: Levels are assigned from the consequence of each defect and are stated independently of any reviewer's rubric: a reachable security or authorization failure, data loss, a broken consumer contract, injection, or a broken deploy gate is error; a degraded behavior, an ambiguous gap, or a misleading-but-not-inverted signal is warning. Private evaluator material: the fixture carries no annotation of any kind. Each finding is anchored at the offending statement in the HEAD version of its file, and the harness matches on path, SARIF level, and line within line_tolerance. Levels follow the skill's severity mapping (CRITICAL/HIGH -> error, MEDIUM -> warning, LOW -> note). requires_reading lists the unchanged files a reviewer must open before the impact is visible; non_findings documents the decoys, the pre-existing defects, and the defect introduced and reverted inside the range, none of which may be reported.

findings.title: The shared egress wrapper stopped validating its target
findings.impact: fetchGuarded no longer rejects internal or non-https targets while every existing caller still relies on it, so a tenant-configured webhook URL reaches the internal network (SSRF). The commit message claims validation moved to the call sites; no call site was changed.

findings.title: Invoice cache key lost its tenant segment
findings.impact: The tenantId parameter is now unused, so two tenants holding the same invoice id share a cache entry. The unchanged read path caches and serves whatever landed first, which is cross-tenant disclosure.

findings.title: Key rotation endpoint is registered without a role guard
findings.impact: The sibling route declares requireRole("staff"); this one does not, so any authenticated tenant user can rotate a workspace signing key and read the new secret from the response. The handler landed 19 commits earlier and was unreachable until this commit registered it.

findings.title: findInvoice dropped its tenant parameter while callers still pass it
findings.impact: The unchanged callers still invoke findInvoice(db, tenantId, invoiceId), so the tenant id is used as the invoice id and the invoice id is read as options. Single invoice reads break, and the query itself is no longer tenant scoped.

findings.title: New NOT NULL column has no default and no backfill
findings.impact: The migration fails on any non-empty invoices table, and the unchanged insertInvoice never supplies currency, so invoice creation breaks after deploy.

findings.title: Invoice payload renamed while the console still reads snake_case
findings.impact: The unchanged console reads total_cents and created_at, so amounts render as NaN and dates disappear. The documented convention is snake_case on the wire.

findings.title: Shared request timeout disabled for every service
findings.impact: The transport treats 0 as no timeout, so the unchanged billing job and webhook delivery can hang on an unresponsive provider and hold their workers indefinitely.

findings.title: Inbound webhook route lost its integration role guard
findings.impact: Any authenticated tenant user can now publish forged inbound webhook events to the queue, which downstream consumers treat as provider traffic.

findings.title: Message is acknowledged before it is processed
findings.impact: The consumer turned at-least-once delivery into at-most-once: a handler failure or crash silently drops the message instead of redelivering it. Queued billing work is lost with no operator signal, which is a blocking regression rather than a tuning concern.

findings.title: Fork code runs with repository secrets
findings.impact: pull_request_target grants the workflow the base repository token and secrets, and the job then checks out the pull request head and runs its scripts, so any contributor can exfiltrate COVERAGE_TOKEN or push with write permission.

findings.title: Runtime base image moved from a pinned digest to a floating tag
findings.impact: Builds stop being reproducible and a new upstream image can change the runtime without any repository change.

findings.title: Customer-controlled slug is interpolated into a shell command
findings.impact: loadWorkspace validates only the length of slug, and this job runs from cron with the production database role, so a tenant that names a workspace with shell metacharacters executes arbitrary commands there. The previous version used execFileSync with a fixed argument list.

findings.title: Rejected request body is written to the log
findings.impact: The whole client payload now reaches the log on every validation failure, including any credential or personal field the client sent.

findings.title: Report name falls back to a caller-controlled path segment
findings.impact: An unknown name is no longer rejected: the query value is appended to the report root, so ../ segments read any file the service can reach, including other tenants' report directories.

findings.title: Adjustment write dropped its optimistic concurrency guard
findings.impact: The read-modify-write no longer checks the version it read, so two concurrent operator adjustments silently overwrite each other instead of returning a conflict. A committed write is lost with no error, no conflict and no record that it happened, which is data loss rather than a tuning concern.

findings.title: Assertion was widened to accept the broken rendering
findings.impact: The test now passes when the amount renders as NaN, so it certifies the payload rename instead of catching it. The fixture was also cast to bypass the view's own type.

findings.title: Delivery failures are reported as successful deliveries
findings.impact: The catch block increments the success counter and returns true, so the caller treats a failed delivery as done and never retries while the dashboard shows a total outage as healthy. The misleading signal and the lost delivery together make it blocking.

findings.title: Roles are cached for an hour with no invalidation on revocation
findings.impact: The unchanged revocation path deletes the row and the session entry but not this cache, so a revoked staff role keeps working for up to an hour. An authorization decision that survives its own revocation for an hour is a bypass with a time bound, not a caching preference.

findings.title: Retention sweep deletes every old invoice, not only drafts
findings.impact: and became or, so the nightly cron job deletes every invoice older than the cutoff regardless of status, including issued and paid ones. The log line still claims it purged drafts.

findings.title: Debug endpoints enabled in the production overlay
findings.impact: This overlay carries NODE_ENV=production, so the triage endpoints ship to production with no separate gate or expiry.

findings.title: Role guard became async while its only caller does not await it
findings.impact: The unchanged middleware chain invokes route middleware synchronously, so the returned promise is discarded and every requireRole guard now passes. The rejection surfaces as an unhandled rejection after the response was produced.

non_findings.why: The inline requireAuth calls were removed, but the unchanged global chain in middleware/index.ts authenticates every route.
Operator note is rendered through the unchanged shared sanitizer and the title escapes quotes.
Math.random is retry jitter, not a security decision.
Raw SQL, but parameterized and tenant scoped.
The index is dropped and recreated in the same migration.
Touches production but keeps the environment guard; kubectl diff is read-only.
usageMeterPreview defaults to false; only debugEndpoints is a finding.

SQL concatenation predates main and is untouched by the range.
